reflections.title: "The Unsearchable Riches of Christ"

reflect.text: The apostle Paul saw sharing the good news of Jesus as a great honor, not a chore. Yet carrying out this great task made him deeply humble. When we try to serve Jesus and tell others about him, we quickly realize how weak we are on our own. Like a boat that sinks deeper into the water as it fills up, the more we do for Christ, the more we see our need for him. Through it all, Paul kept his focus entirely on Jesus and the cross.

What Paul proclaimed was the unending treasure found in Jesus. Charles Spurgeon wrote that Christ's riches are "beyond the count of arithmetic" and human imagination. Jesus is always far greater than our highest thoughts of him. He is quicker to forgive us than we are to wander into sin, and he gladly provides everything we need. He gives us peace like a shepherd caring for sheep, caring for us in this life and preparing a home for us with him forever.

questions: When you think about Jesus, do you remember that his mercy is far bigger than your mistakes?
How does serving Jesus help you see your need for his strength?
reflections.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank you for your unending riches of grace and love. Keep us humble as we serve you, and remind us of your great kindness every day. Help us fix our eyes on you and share your goodness with others. Amen.

reflections.title: "Boldness and Confidence"

reflect.text: Because of Jesus, we have direct and welcome access to God at any moment. We never have to clean up our lives first or try to impress him before we pray. Our confidence does not rest on our own good behavior or how well we perform. Instead, our assurance rests entirely on what Jesus has already accomplished for us. Knowing this takes away our fear and turns prayer into an open, honest conversation with God.

In ancient times, worshippers were kept at a distance, but Jesus tore away the barrier between God and us. Today, we can come straight to our heavenly Father with the freedom of deeply loved children. We do not need special rituals or human priests to speak for us. Whenever the enemy whispers that we are too unworthy to pray, Jesus is our credentials. We can step forward with bold hearts because Christ welcomes us in.

questions: Do you ever feel like you need to earn God's approval before talking to him in prayer?
How does knowing that Jesus is your credential give you confidence to approach God today?
reflections.prayer: Father, thank you that we can speak to you freely at any time. Thank you that Jesus tore away every wall and made us your cherished children. When we feel unworthy, help us rest completely in what Christ has done for us. Amen.

D3.author: Whitney Hopler
D3.work: You Have VIP Access to God

reflections.title: God's Wisdom Shown to the Heavens

reflect.text: Paul wrote this letter while locked in prison, yet he urged his friends not to lose heart over his hardships. He knew that God was working out an eternal plan that reaches far beyond what human eyes can see. Even our quiet, hidden struggles are never useless or forgotten. Spiritual beings in the heavenly realms are actively watching the church and seeing the unfolding story of God's grace.

Through the church, God displays his many-sided wisdom to these unseen rulers and authorities. When we choose to trust God in hard moments and praise him through pain, we show the entire cosmos that Jesus is worthy of our devotion. Our faith in times of trial proves that God's love is greater than any earthly comfort. Even when life feels dark, standing firm in Christ carries eternal meaning and brings lasting glory to God.

questions: How does knowing that heavenly powers watch your faith change how you view your personal struggles?
What helps you continue trusting and praising God when your circumstances are difficult?
reflections.prayer: Lord God, thank you that no pain or trial in our lives is ever wasted. When we face dark times, give us the strength to keep trusting and praising you. Let our lives display your great wisdom and glory to all creation. Amen.
